--- title: Missing values description: How polars-umap treats nulls, NaN and infinite values. jupyter: python3 bread-crumbs: false --- A row is **invalid** when it is null, or contains a null, NaN or infinite value. UMAP can't place such a row, so polars-umap gives you two options through `null_policy`. ::: {#7df0592f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.filter(pl.int_range(pl.len()).is_in([3, 10, 20])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
shape: (3, 1)
embedding
array[f64, 3]
null
[1.0, null, 2.0]
[1.0, NaN, 2.0]
``` ::: ::: ## `null_policy="error"` (default) Invalid rows raise an error that says how many there are and where the first one is: ::: {#d2367ebd .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.select(pl.col("embedding").umap.fit_transform()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: ## `null_policy="ignore"` UMAP is fitted on the valid rows only, and the invalid rows get a null result. The output still has one row per input row, so it lines up with the rest of the frame: ::: {#26dc160f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} out = df.with_columns( xy=pl.col("embedding").umap.fit_transform(null_policy="ignore", random_state=0) ) out.filter(pl.col("xy").is_null()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: The valid rows get exactly the embedding they would get if the invalid rows weren't there. ## Nearest neighbors `knn()` supports the same policy. Ignored rows get a null result, and they never appear as someone else's neighbor: ::: {#caecd0a9 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.select(pl.col("embedding").umap.knn(k=3, null_policy="ignore")).head(5) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip} ## Zero vectors and cosine distance An all-zero vector has no direction, so its cosine distance to anything is undefined. Text embeddings of empty documents are a common source of them. Turn them into nulls first: ```python df.with_columns( pl.when( pl.col("embedding").arr.to_list().list.eval(pl.element().abs()).list.sum() > 0 ).then(pl.col("embedding")) ) ``` :::
